positive_class_why: Minority class (37%) and the clinically relevant one.

missing_indicators.why: No missing values in train or test.

categorical_missing.why: No categorical columns; kept for completeness.

zero_as_missing.why: The 11 rows that are zero in all six concavity columns are all benign: a cell contour with no concave segments genuinely has concavity 0, so zero is a real measurement, not a sentinel (house rule: keep physically meaningful zeros).

high_correlation.why: Size measures (radius/perimeter/area, mean/worst) are highly correlated (r up to 0.998); L2 regularisation handles it, but coefficients and importances are shared.

cv.why: 455 training rows: 10 folds lower the variance of the CV estimate (house rule n<2000). Minority share 37% is above the 35% imbalance threshold, so ROC-AUC (ranking quality over both classes) is the primary metric.

threshold.why: Near-balanced classes and unknown costs: maximise balanced accuracy on out-of-fold predictions.

models.label: Logistic Regression

log_transform.why: Seven 'error' columns have skew >= 2 and are non-negative; log1p makes their effect on the logit less dominated by a few large cells.

drop_columns.why: mean perimeter is reconstructable from the other columns with R^2 = 0.9997 (perimeter ~ 2*pi*radius): redundant for a linear model.

models.why: Interpretable linear baseline; tests whether a weighted sum of morphology measures separates the classes. Stopping: lbfgs gradient tolerance 1e-4.

models.label: Random Forest
models.why: Flexible non-linear model. House rule n_train < 1000: Random Forest instead of gradient boosting, because early stopping would hold out ~45 rows. No stopping criterion is needed: 300 trees fixed, more trees average more but do not over-fit; depth and leaf size are tuned instead.

ablations.question: LR: no log transform of skewed error columns
LR: keep the redundant mean perimeter
